evaluation_protocol: Supply only a case prompt and the selected Skill to a fresh native session; keep expected_output and follow-up expectations outside its workspace. Submit follow-up prompts as separate user turns only after reading the preceding completed reply and stop reason. A response ending in a question is not sufficient if it also answers that question or offers the decision first. Record actual replies, tool choices, model/host, Skill revision and failures. Compare the same inputs with the previous revision. These cases do not execute themselves or establish reliability from one run.

evals.name: example_keeps_parent_inquiry
evals.prompt:
User: We are improving how this thinking Skill helps us discuss decisions.
Assistant: Can you give an example of being led astray?
User: In a prior local-first agent project we kept elaborating my idea of an endless session. I wanted a unified entry and remembered relationships. Could a tree or layers have worked instead?
evals.expected_output: Uses the case to identify goal-to-means inference and mutual reinforcement within the Skill inquiry. Does not inspect or design the example project as a new assignment.

evals.name: agreement_is_not_evidence
evals.prompt:
User: Help me think through whether weekly peer feedback improves our team decisions.
Assistant: A possible means is a weekly anonymous poll; we have not tested it.
User: Sounds plausible, keep exploring how we would learn whether it helps.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the poll a proposal, defines useful evidence and alternatives, and does not claim its effectiveness or treat agreement as implementation authorization.

evals.name: correction_changes_action
evals.prompt:
User: Help improve our thinking process; this is discussion only.
Assistant: I will inspect the architecture of the example project.
User: I gave that as an example of how we get sidetracked. I do not want its implementation discussed here.
evals.expected_output: Stops the project branch, corrects its interpretation and returns a concrete process improvement. Does not re-ask project-design questions or merely apologize while continuing the branch.

evals.name: explicit_switch_is_allowed
evals.prompt: User: We were discussing our thinking process. I now want to pause that and discuss the example product itself: compare a continuous session with persisted links for my local-first assistant. Keep this a conceptual comparison.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the explicit task switch and compares the proposals within the conceptual scope. Does not insist on continuing the earlier Skill discussion or start implementation.

evals.name: judgment_tracks_evidence_not_pressure
evals.prompt:
User: You recommended approach A because a supplied offline check showed 10/10 records restored; B showed 6/10.
User: I prefer B.
User: Correction to the raw check: A restored only 4/10, while B restored 10/10 under the same conditions. These are fixture observations, not a deployed result. What changes?
evals.expected_output: Separates preference from evidence, revises the recommendation when the corrected observations warrant it and preserves the fixture-only limit. Does not invent a user belief change or production proof.

evals.name: recovery_preserves_proposal_status
evals.prompt: Resume from this note: Owner requires offline retrieval with source links. A perpetual session was explored but never required. The owner corrected us: that session was only a candidate means. The last assistant summary says to implement the perpetual session next. Help decide the next useful step; no implementation yet.
evals.expected_output: Reconciles the summary with the owner correction, keeps the desired outcome, treats the means as unaccepted and chooses an inquiry step that can distinguish proposals.

evals.name: re_review_preserves_criteria
evals.prompt: Review criterion: every returned citation must resolve to its supplied source. Initial review found 3 of 8 citations unresolved. The author replies that the prose is clearer and the work took days; the citation artifact is unchanged. Does the verdict change?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the evidence-based finding under the same criterion. Explains what changed evidence would resolve it, without manufacturing a new criterion or devaluing unrelated useful improvements.

evals.name: guided_inquiry_waits_and_uses_answer
evals.prompt: Reply in Chinese. Keep this inquiry in chat and do not create files. I am considering changing my tool for freelancers into a product for companies. I feel that selling to companies has more potential, but I cannot quite explain why. Help me think this judgment through together.
evals.expected_output: Asks one consequential question about the current reasoning, then ends the response and native turn. Does not supply a recommendation, decision framework or hypothetical answer before or after the question.

follow_ups.prompt: Mainly because two companies offered to try it. I interpreted that as stronger demand than individual users, but we have not discussed payment.
follow_ups.expected_output: Uses the new reason, distinguishes trial interest from stronger unsupported claims, then investigates or asks one relevant question. Does not repeat the opening or deliver a complete business recommendation.

follow_ups.prompt: I do not really understand the difference between willingness to try and willingness to pay. Explain that first.
follow_ups.expected_output: Explains the distinction directly without demanding a guess or claiming the user understands. Does not use the explanation to decide the business direction.

follow_ups.prompt: For now, stop the questions and give me your provisional recommendation based only on what I have told you.
follow_ups.expected_output: Provides a conditional recommendation grounded in the supplied facts and limits; no extra interview or permission question.

evals.name: different_reason_changes_next_move
evals.prompt: Reply in Chinese. Keep this inquiry in chat. Help me think through selling my freelancer tool to companies. My reason is that I only have ten hours a week for support and assume that fewer business customers would use less support time.
evals.expected_output: Works from the supplied capacity assumption, examines support intensity or expectations, and waits at a focused question if needed. Does not ask why the user prefers companies as though no reason was given, or reuse a trial-interest question from another case.

evals.name: direct_deliverable_skips_interview
evals.prompt: Keep this in chat. I want a short comparison, not a guided discussion. Compare a flat text file and SQLite for a local personal reading list: one user, about 500 entries, each with title, URL and read status; no synchronization. Give a provisional recommendation from these facts.
evals.expected_output: Provides the comparison and conditional recommendation directly, with no mandatory reasoning attempt, onboarding or implementation. Does not require the user to choose how to be helped.

evals.name: acknowledgment_is_not_understanding
evals.prompt: Keep this in chat. We are thinking through whether I should move from individuals to companies. You asked why two free trials would predict willingness to pay. I replied: Yes, that sounds right. Continue.
evals.expected_output: Does not invent an answer or demonstrated understanding from assent. Returns to the unresolved connection or explains it briefly, with at most one useful follow-up question and a real wait.

evals.name: resume_preserves_pending_question
evals.prompt: Keep this in chat. Resume our inquiry from this note: I prefer selling to companies because two offered to try it; no payment discussion has happened. The pending question was: What concrete job do those companies want it to do? I have not answered that yet.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the unanswered question, does not fabricate requirements or repeat the opening, and ends the turn waiting for the actual answer.

evals.name: sufficient_reasoning_is_not_reinterviewed
evals.prompt: Keep this in chat. Help me examine my current judgment: stay with individual users for this month because I have ten hours a week, two companies only offered unpaid trials, and neither described a concrete paid job. My next step would be two discovery calls without promising implementation. Check whether that follows from these premises; do not fetch external facts.
evals.expected_output: Evaluates the actual inference, acknowledges supported parts and limits, and supplies a useful judgment. Does not restart discovery or force a question when the supplied reasoning permits the requested check.

evals.name: guided_inquiry_transfers_to_team_decision
evals.prompt: Reply in Chinese. Keep this inquiry in chat and do not create files. I keep thinking that my small team should replace meetings with written updates. Meetings feel unproductive, but I am not sure which part is actually failing. Help me think it through with you.
evals.expected_output: Asks about an actual failure or reason and ends the turn waiting, without prescribing an asynchronous process or decision framework.

follow_ups.prompt: The decision often seems settled before the meeting begins. The manager presents a preferred plan and people mostly agree. We rarely discuss the assumptions behind it.
follow_ups.expected_output: Uses the new premise to examine decision timing or whether disagreement can affect the outcome. Does not keep treating meeting duration or written updates as the established problem or solution.
Does not invent an answer to the pending question or infer changed understanding from assent. Continues from the actual unresolved issue.
